ui.title: Hershey — Labor Day Weekend 2026
ui.origin: All distances and drive times are from the Hersheypark entrance
ui.noteTicket: ⏰ Happy Hours Ticket: park entry from 5:00 pm to close. Evenings are already spoken for — everything here is a morning or early-afternoon plan. Bonus: with that ticket ZooAmerica is free if you enter from inside the park.
ui.noteHours: Hours: the ones marked ✓ confirmed came from the venue's own website. The ⚠ check ones are estimates — call ahead or check Google Maps. ⭐ Star ratings are for reference; the "Maps + reviews" button opens Google Maps with the real ones.
ui.footNote: Distances and drive times computed with OSRM over OpenStreetMap data · map © OpenStreetMap · hours and events from each venue's own website · star ratings from Google Maps (reference). Photos from each venue's own site or from Wikimedia/Wikipedia — swipe the image to see more.

ui.agendaSub: One plan per day, built around the Happy Hours ticket. Nothing here is booked — swap whatever you want.

agenda.Llegada — la mayoría sale del trabajo: Arrival — most of us are coming straight from work

agenda.Abre 9am–5pm. Ir temprano y salir con ti: Open 9am–5pm. Go early and leave yourself time.

Hershey's Chocolate World.price: FREE entry and ride · Create Your Own Bar $27 · Trolley $24
Hershey's Chocolate World.why: The chocolate tour ride is FREE, runs 10 min, and they hand you chocolate at the end. Huge store.
Hershey's Chocolate World.tip: Cheapest thing all weekend: the free ride. Go early — after 11am it's a mob.

ZooAmerica.price: $16 adult · $13 child · FREE with a Hersheypark ticket
ZooAmerica.why: 11-acre zoo with North American animals only: bears, wolves, bobcat, alligators, owls.
ZooAmerica.tip: Free entry from inside Hersheypark with your Happy Hours ticket. Use it.

The Hershey Story Museum.price: Museum $17 adult / $13 child · Chocolate Lab $22 · Tasting $15
The Hershey Story Museum.why: The story of Milton Hershey. The Chocolate Lab (you make your own bar) and the tasting of chocolates from 4 countries are the best parts.
The Hershey Story Museum.tip: The Chocolate Lab fills up — book online NOW, not at the door.

YAH Brew.why: Small taproom in downtown Hershey. Quick, casual, walkable from the center.

Jazz at the Barnyard.why: Live outdoor jazz at the historic barn. Intimate — bring a folding chair.
Jazz at the Barnyard.tip: Clashes with the park's Happy Hours on Friday. Pick one.
Jazz at the Barnyard.event: 🎷 FRIDAY 4: Third Stream band concert, 7–9pm. Gates and the photo exhibit open at 6pm.

Through the Lens of Hershey.why: Historic Hershey photography exhibit. Short, and air-conditioned.
Through the Lens of Hershey.tip: 30–45 min. Perfect for killing time if it rains.
Through the Lens of Hershey.event: 📸 Photography by John Martin. Fri 4 preview night (6–9pm, during the Jazz) and Sat 5 Gallery Day (10am–3pm).

Hershey Gardens.why: 23 acres of themed gardens + a Butterfly Atrium with hundreds of butterflies flying loose + an interactive Children's Garden.
Hershey Gardens.tip: Hit the butterfly atrium first — they're more active in the morning. 1.5–2 h.
Hershey Gardens.event: 🎨 Fri 4 to Sun 6: Hershey Area Art Association Show & Sale ('Blooming Art'), 9am–6pm. Friday 12–12:30pm: live feeding at the Zoology Zone.

Hidden Still Spirits.why: Local whiskey, rum and vodka distillery. Serious cocktails in a speakeasy-ish bar.
Hidden Still Spirits.tip: Grown-up room — not the plan with kids.

Rotunda Brew Pub.why: Brewpub inside the Hershey Lodge. Convenient and close, at hotel prices.
Rotunda Brew Pub.tip: Worst value on the list. Only if you're wiped out and don't want to drive.

Tröegs Independent Brewing.why: The #1 brewery in the area. Huge industrial hall, a snack bar with good food, and a FREE self-guided tour down hallways with windows onto production.
Tröegs Independent Brewing.tip: If you do ONE brewery, this one. Genuinely kid-friendly — whole families in there.
Tröegs Independent Brewing.event: 🍺 Open on Labor Day Monday with special hours (11:30am–9pm).

AACA Automobile Museum.why: First-rate classic car museum. Cars from the 1890s to today, buses, and the Tucker exhibit. Big, and air-conditioned.
AACA Automobile Museum.tip: The #1 rain plan. Easily 2 h inside.
AACA Automobile Museum.event: 🚗 SATURDAY 5: Duryea Day (antique car show, 9am–3pm) + Ollie Day (9am–5pm) + the talk 'Board Tracks: Speed, Spectacle & Risk in Early Auto Racing'.

Rubber Soul Brewing.why: Small brewpub with its own kitchen in historic downtown Hummelstown. Beatles theme.
Rubber Soul Brewing.tip: Perfect combo: Indian Echo Caverns in the morning, lunch here (5 min away).

Cocoa Kayak Rentals.why: Easy float down Swatara Creek, no rapids. They shuttle you upstream and pick you up.
Cocoa Kayak Rentals.tip: Book NOW — Labor Day sells out. Depends on water level, so call if it hasn't rained.

Indian Echo Caverns.why: Limestone cave at a steady 52°F. 45-minute guided tour. Outside there's gem mining and farm animals for the kids.
Indian Echo Caverns.tip: The #1 pick on a hot day. Bring a sweater — it's genuinely cold inside. Wet, slippery floor.

Snitz Creek Brewery.why: Unpretentious local brewery, among the best prices around. Not touristy at all.

The Vineyard at Hershey.why: Vineyard with its own wines and beers, live music, and a big patio looking over the vines.
The Vineyard at Hershey.tip: Open space — works well for a big group with kids running around.

Reservoir Park.why: The highest point in Harrisburg — view of the skyline and the Capitol dome. You drive right to the top, zero hiking.
Reservoir Park.tip: Lookout for the lazy: park and you're there. Good at sunset.

Mt. Gretna Lake & Beach.why: Lake with an imported sand beach, water slide, floating trampoline and snack bar. 1950s summer-town vibe.
Mt. Gretna Lake & Beach.tip: HEADS UP: the last day of the season is normally Labor Day. CALL before you drive out.
Mt. Gretna Lake & Beach.event: 🏖️ Labor Day Monday is usually the LAST day of the season. Call first.

Coleman Memorial Park.why: Big municipal park with a giant playground, pool, courts and shaded picnic areas.
Coleman Memorial Park.tip: Cheap way to burn off the kids' energy without paying anything.

Pennsylvania State Capitol.why: One of the most beautiful capitols in the U.S. — gilded dome modeled on St. Peter's, marble staircase, murals. Teddy Roosevelt called it 'the handsomest building I ever saw'.
Pennsylvania State Capitol.tip: Free and spectacular. Confirm whether it opens on Labor Day Monday. Pair it with Kipona.

Boyd Big Tree Preserve.why: 1,000 acres of mature forest with huge trees. Trails from easy to a climb up the ridge.
Boyd Big Tree Preserve.tip: Full shade — the best pick on a hot day.

Second Mountain Hawk Watch.why: Rocky overlook above the valley. Early September = peak hawk and eagle migration. You can almost drive all the way up.
Second Mountain Hawk Watch.tip: Little walking, big view. Bring binoculars if you have them.

Memorial Lake State Park.why: 85-acre lake with a flat 1.5-mile loop trail, picnic tables, fishing. Very quiet and close by.
Memorial Lake State Park.tip: Easiest park on the list with kids. Bring food and make it a picnic.

Kipona Festival.why: The biggest event of the weekend. Food, crafts, live music, craft beer and a Native American powwow along the Susquehanna River.
Kipona Festival.tip: City Island parking fills up — get there before noon, or park downtown and walk across the pedestrian bridge.
Kipona Festival.event: 🎉 110th Kipona · Family Fun Zone, Giant Puppet Parade, Keystone Dock Dogs, Art in the Park, food trucks, beer/wine garden. FIREWORKS on Sunday. Metered parking FREE Sunday and Monday; $5 at the River Street Garage on Saturday 8am–5pm.

Cornwall Iron Furnace.why: The only intact 18th-century iron furnace in the Western Hemisphere. National historic site, small and unusual.
Cornwall Iron Furnace.tip: 45 min. Fits nicely on the way to Mt. Gretna or Governor Dick.

Wildwood Park.why: Lake with a wooden boardwalk over the wetland, turtles, herons and lotus flowers. Flat 3-mile trail — you can do just a piece of it.
Wildwood Park.tip: Strollers roll fine. Pair it with Kipona (10 min away).

Fort Hunter Mansion & Park.why: An 1814 mansion above the Susquehanna, with gardens, a barn and a riverside trail. Gorgeous river view.
Fort Hunter Mansion & Park.tip: The park alone is worth it and it's free. The mansion is optional.

Governor Dick Observation Tower.why: THE BEST LOOKOUT around. A 66-foot concrete tower you climb by interior stairs — 360° view over 4 counties. About a 1-mile hike each way through woods, moderate.
Governor Dick Observation Tower.tip: Best thing all weekend and it's free. Bring water and closed shoes. It's dark inside the tower — use your phone flashlight.

Swatara State Park.why: 3,500 acres. Flat gravel rail-trail for walking or biking, the creek to dip your feet in, and Devonian fossils in the road cut.
Swatara State Park.tip: Fossil area: kids find real trilobites. You're allowed to take them.

Hawk Rock Overlook.why: Appalachian Trail hike up to a rock with a view of the Susquehanna River and the town of Duncannon.
Hawk Rock Overlook.tip: ~1.2 mi each way, steep. Not for little kids or for a hot day.

Downtown Lititz.price: Walking FREE · Julius Sturgis Pretzel tour $6
Downtown Lititz.why: Voted 'America's coolest small town'. A main street from the 1750s, the country's oldest pretzel factory (you twist your own), the Wilbur chocolate shop, and a park with a creek.
Downtown Lititz.tip: Prettiest stroll on the list. A full half-day. Many shops close on Sunday.
Downtown Lititz.event: 🛍️ Fri 4 and Sat 5: 'Thanks for the Love Party' at Bunyaad Marketplace — 20% off everything.

Waggoner's Gap Hawk Watch.why: Legendary Audubon lookout on the Blue Mountain ridge. In September hundreds of raptors pass through daily. Huge view of the Cumberland Valley.
Waggoner's Gap Hawk Watch.tip: Short but rocky climb from the parking lot. Farthest place on this list.
